proposals.before: The commentary says: After Prince Limi was deposed, from Princes Yinqi and Yin'e to the great ministers, many plotted to install Yinshi, but the Sacred Ancestor never permitted it.
proposals.after: The commentary says: After Prince Limi was deposed, from Princes Yintang and Yin'e to the great ministers, many plotted to install Yinshi, but the Sacred Ancestor never permitted it.
proposals.reason: 允禟 is conventionally Yintang (or Yinsi), not Yinqi; Yinqi misreads the personal name.

proposals.before: Tong Guowei · Ma Qi (Fuliang; Ma Wu; Baozhu) · A Ling A (Aersong'a) · Kui Xu · E Lundai
proposals.after: Tong Guowei · Ma Qi (Fuliang; Ma Wu; Baozhu) · Aringa (Aersong'a) · Kui Xu · Olondai
proposals.reason: Chapter body consistently uses Aringa and Olondai; title line A Ling A / E Lundai are nonstandard splits of the same names.

decisions.reason: Chinese 允禟 is Yintang; Yinqi misreads a different imperial name (允祺). The proposed replacement corrects only that personal name and leaves the rest of the idiomatic intact.

阿靈阿 and 鄂倫岱 are accurately rendered by the syllable-spaced A Ling A and E Lundai; switching to Aringa/Olondai is a romanization-style preference for consistency, not a semantic correction of the Chinese.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Yinqi (and matching pinyin) came only from misreading 允禟; the personal-name claim must read Yintang while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
